name: Macsen Wledig
text: Macsen Wledig is the Welsh title of the Roman commander Magnus Maximus. A Middle Welsh tale uses the name Macsen. In that tale a Roman emperor dreams of a lady in a far country. He sees in sleep a fair valley, a tower, and the face of the woman. He sends his men across the land until they find the lady Elen in a rich castle in Wales. Everything he meets on waking matches what he saw. He grants her father the rule of the island and makes a bridal home for her. In his absence a rival claims the city and the throne. Led by Elen's own kin, Macsen crosses the water and wins Rome back. He rewards his men with a western land that becomes the later Brittany. The tale reads as a study of kingship and of the land. The true Maximus ruled the west from the year 383 to the year 388. The title remained among the Welsh folk for the great ruler.

attributes.attribute: The Welsh name for the Roman commander Magnus Maximus
The lady of the dream who becomes his bride
The western land that his followers later held

okr.objective: Document Mac Wledig as the Welsh portrait of Maximus.
key_results: Set the dream-tale of Macsen in Middle Welsh.
Join Maximus to the figure of the dream.
Trace the western land given to the British host.
